subject: Archaeology
title: Pearl Harbor: Underwater Memorial
description: A fast breakdown of Pearl Harbor: Underwater Memorial for builders.

hook.text: The USS Arizona has been leaking oil since it sank on December 7, 1941. Visitors call the drops 'black tears.'

buildup.text: Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor sank or damaged 21 ships and killed 2,403 Americans in under two hours.

discovery.text: The Arizona was never raised. A memorial was built directly above the sunken hull, which is visible through the water.

twist.text: The ship still holds an estimated 500,000 gallons of fuel oil. A slow leak could become an environmental disaster.

climax.text: Corrosion is weakening the hull. The Navy monitors it constantly, balancing preservation with ecological risk.

punchline.text: The Arizona still bleeds oil 80 years later. The war is not over for the ship.

quiz.question: What ongoing risk does the USS Arizona wreck pose?
options: Unexploded ammunition could detonate at any time
Corrosion could cause a collapse releasing 500,000 gallons of fuel oil
The memorial structure above is sinking into the wreck
